sections.html: Tyttocharax species are among the smallest tetras of all. They hardly ever grow larger than 2 cm. Available size: 1–1.5 cm.
Peru. Two species are currently imported quite often, both from Peru: T. cochui and T. madeirae.
Any usual fish food is readily taken as long as it fits the mouth.
Keeping these tiny fish is not very demanding. The dwarf fish are very peaceful towards tankmates, whether of their own or other species. Plants are not harmed.
Males become larger than the females and are very deep bodied at age.

T. cochui and T. madeirae look very similar at first glance and have often been confused in the past. T. madeirae has not been recognized in scientific collections from Peru so far. They are best distinguished by the coloration of the dorsal and anal fins: both fins are hyaline in T. cochui and have dark markings in T. madeirae.

Name: Tyttocharax means ancient Greek “tiny Charax”; Charax is another genus of tetra. cochui is a dedication name. madeirae refers to the Rio Madeira in Brazil.

Suggested common names: T. cochui: Whiteband Frippery Tetra; T. madeirae: Madeira Frippery Tetra.
